newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cambodia's Rainsy wants aid money suspended.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Rainsy wants aid money suspended.

text.p: Cambodian opposition figure Sam Rainsy urged the international community on Monday to cut off financial aid to Phnom Penh following Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's ouster of First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh.
"The coup d'etat staged over the weekend by the Second Prime Minister Hun Sen must be clearly condemned," Rainsy said.
"Any assistance to Cambodia through the illegal government of Phnom Penh -- especially loans provided by the World Bank and used as budget support -- must be interrupted," Rainsy said in a statement.
He said only social aid programmes implemented through non-governmental organisations should be maintained.
A Ranariddh ally and former Cambodian finance minister who heads the officially unrecognised Khmer Nation Party, Rainsy was on holiday in Nimes, southern France.
Ranariddh, who fled Cambodia for southern France on Friday, told Reuters on Monday that his rival Hun Sen, had ousted him from power and vowed to organise resistance against him around the world.

Ranariddh left the day before fighting broke out in the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh when Hun Sen ordered a crackdown on "illegal troops" under Ranariddh's command. Hun Sen took complete control of the capital and its outskirts on Monday.
The two men had shared power as co-heads of a fractured and unwieldy coalition government formed after a United Nations-run election in 1993.
Donor nations and institutions meeting at World Bank offices in Paris last week had pledged $450 million in official aid to Cambodia for 1997-98.
But the donors had warned Phnom Penh to ensure that political issues did not destabilise the gains made since 1993.
